html:
Kickapoo (Oklahoma) marks the land of the Kickapoo Tribe of Oklahoma, around McLoud, east of Oklahoma City. The Kickapoo are an Algonquian people from the Great Lakes, first known in what is now Wisconsin.

Over two centuries they moved south and west, through Illinois, Missouri and Kansas, often refusing to settle where the United States wanted them. In the 1850s many went to northern Mexico, where Mexico gave them land in Coahuila in return for guarding the frontier. In the 1870s and 1880s part of this group was brought back and given a reservation in Indian Territory. That reservation was split into allotments in the 1890s and the rest opened to settlers. Neighbouring tribal lands include those of the Potawatomi and Shawnee and the Sac and Fox.
